content_html:
The Probabilistic Brain

Microscale → Coding/Representation → Systems/Dynamics

The brain is probabilistic because biophysics is noisy (ion channels, synapses), and because evolution harnessed this variability to encode and compute with uncertainty (population codes, Bayesian inference), producing stochastic network dynamics that are robust, adaptive, and efficient.

Why this is useful

Robustness: Distributed, probabilistic codes tolerate failures at individual synapses/neurons.
Efficient decisions: Bayesian-like combination of prior knowledge with uncertain evidence explains perception under ambiguity.
Exploration & learning: Stochasticity supports credit assignment and avoids overfitting to noisy inputs.
